I'd go with the fallback version. It's the more useful of the two while still being honest with me. When it couldn't fetch the page's details, it didn't just leave me staring at a blank box — it put the site's name in as a stand-in so I've got something recognizable and can save right away, and it told me plainly that's what it did and that I can adjust it first. So I'm never misled into thinking it grabbed the real title; it's upfront that this is a placeholder from the address.

The manual version was honest too, but making me come up with a title from scratch before I'm allowed to save is more work at exactly the moment something already went a bit wrong. The fallback lets me save the thing now and tidy the wording later if I care to.

The one thing I'd hold onto from both is that either way I can still type my own title over it — which the fallback clearly lets me do. So: use the site name as a sensible stand-in, say so honestly, and let me save immediately or rename it. That's the one I want.
